Add the Unity SDK, Valheim and Rust plugins, RCON server control and an installer

Unity SDK (C#, BepInEx-agnostic): JSON, mailbox, coroutine RPC server, observe-mode
humanoid discovery with bone resolution (Humanoid avatar, name patterns for
Mixamo/Valheim/Rust/UE-style rigs, profile overrides), a free camera rendering
to a RenderTexture, Camera.WorldToScreenPoint probes, Physics raycast visibility.
Game members (Valheim EnvMan, ZNetScene, Player) are reached by reflection so the
plugins build without any game assembly. Rust: client observes, the core controls
time/weather on the own local server over RCON (stdlib WebSocket client, templated
commands from the profile). `dataopen install` copies the GMod addon or builds and
installs the BepInEx plugin. The C# cannot be compiled in CI here: it is parsed
(tree-sitter) and checked for C# 7.3 and protocol-key conformance instead.

Add the shared Lua runtime and a Lua mock game, tested on Lua 5.1/5.4/LuaJIT

dataopen_rpc.lua speaks protocol v1 from inside a game (JSON, mailbox polling,
coroutine handlers with wait_frames/wait_until, bone-name resolution with
weights and profile overrides, engine-vs-core projection probes, freeze
watchdog, handler timeout, staged image commit for sandboxed mods). A game mod
only supplies engine bindings. The runtime is exercised end to end (doctor,
collection, verify) against a Lua simulated game with inch units and
ValveBiped names, driven by the real Python core, on lupa lua51/lua54/luajit.

Add doctor, verify, preview, merge, game profiles and a unified CLI

doctor: ladder of integration checks (connect, mod self-tests, spawn, engine-vs-core
projection probes with cause diagnosis, centimeter-unit detection, bone-length
sanity, left/right swap, image size/blank frame, negative frame, throughput)
with skeleton overlays and concrete fix hints. verify: cross-checks canonical
JSONL, image sizes, YOLO and COCO files and reports coverage statistics.
Profiles are TOML data (mailbox path, render size, capture mode, mod options,
bone overrides, provenance). collect runs the doctor first and refuses on FAIL.

Fix found by verify: labels rounded to 2 decimals could land exactly on the frame
edge (319.996 -> 320.00); points within 0.01px of the edge are now out of frame.

Add remote adapter, mock game server and harden the orchestrator

RemoteGameAdapter drives a game mod over the mailbox protocol with engine-side
or host-side (screen grab) image capture; the mock game now speaks the wire
protocol so the whole stack runs end to end without a game.

Orchestrator: engine-vs-core projection probe check with automatic diagnosis
(flipped Y/X, focal/FOV mismatch) and CalibrationError; aborts loudly on
persistent adapter failure instead of finishing with an empty dataset; commits
labels for frames saved before a mid-scene failure; graceful stop; shard
index/count for parallel game instances; self-occlusion wired into the
annotation builder; DATASET_CARD.json with provenance placeholder.

Add TurfTab: split turf fees and track who has paid

Next.js 16 + Neon Postgres + Drizzle app for splitting a weekly football
ground rent equally among the players who actually played.

- Games with multiple cost items; per-head charge rounds up, surplus shown
- Ledger model: balances derived from charges and payments, never stored
- One-tap mark paid, partial payments, undo; oldest-game-first allocation
- Group share page (no balances) and per-player personal links
- Admin auth via env password, signed session cookie, login lockout,
  proxy redirect plus requireAdmin() on every page and action
- CSV export, installable PWA with offline page
- Unit tests for split, ledger, session and CSV logic

Add "My games" lists, show them on player cards, let creators delete campaigns

My games:
- Each player keeps a list of favourite / owned games (up to 60) on their
  profile (players/{id}.games), managed from a "Manage my games" button in the
  profile: search or paste a link to add, X to remove.
- When adding a game to a day, the player's list shows first (minus games
  already on that day); typing shows matching own games before the game list.
- A player's card shows their list under their name as links to BoardGameGeek
  (short lists start open, over 8 start closed).
- New js/mygames.js (pure helpers, tested), cached by the service worker.

Campaigns: the creator (or a signed-in admin) can now remove a campaign,
running or finished, after a confirmation. Its sessions stay in the hall of fame.

firestore.rules: players may store a games list (max 60); campaign delete is
no longer admin-only (the creator-only part is enforced by the site, since the
rules cannot tell who is who). Must be re-published in the console.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add campaigns, last week preview, player cards, campaign banners

Campaigns tab (teal) for long games played over several sessions:
- Start a campaign; anyone can join (and leave) until the creator locks it,
  after which only the creator adds people. Creator can unlock again.
- Anyone in a campaign logs sessions and picks the next day right in the
  log popup; "Plan next session" does the same later and shows on the calendar.
- Only the creator (or a signed-in admin) can finish a campaign, and reopen a
  finished one. Finished campaigns are tinted grey with a dashed edge.
- Running campaigns sit in their own collapsible list; each campaign's
  sessions list is collapsed by default and shows dates and notes only.
- Slim orange banners on the calendar for a game night or a campaign session
  today/tomorrow, each with a link to the day or to the campaign.

Also: collapsible "Last week" preview so unlogged game nights can still be
logged, and player cards (stats and titles) opened from any player name.

firestore.rules: new campaigns collection (people, lock, next day, finish,
reopen), campaign/note fields on plays. Must be re-published in the console.

Add stand-alone ESP32 chess clock for Waveshare AMOLED-1.8 (V2)

Two-player touch chess clock: top half drawn upside down, tap your own half
to pass the turn. 12 time controls with Fischer increment, pause/restart/menu,
flag screen, seven-segment display with tenths under 20 s. Never dims during a
game (running or paused).

- src/clock.h: pure C++ game logic with host tests (tests/test_clock.cpp)
- src/main.cpp: CO5300 display, CST820 touch on its own task, power policy
- tools/board.sh, tools/ctl.py: build/flash/revert wrapper; serial test driver
  with tap simulation, state readout, touch calibration and PNG screenshots
- Touch is mapped from the CST820's raw window to screen coordinates (fitted
  from a 9-point calibration screen)

Playful motion for children and an app icon that matches the mascot

Motion (all of it off under prefers-reduced-motion): marking an ayah makes
its button jump and throw a few stars; 'I memorised the whole surah' sends
a wave of jumping stars down the page; right game answers hop and throw
stars; unlocked medals and today's goal stars pop in when a page opens.
A newly unlocked medal is announced ('وسام جديد'), detected by comparing
what was unlocked before and after each change, per child. Celebrations
and medal notices now go through a queue so a medal never hides the
'surah completed' message (checked: medal, medal, then the completion
message, in order). Under reduced motion the text still appears, with no
movement.

Icon: favicon, 192/512, maskable (kept inside the safe zone) and the
iOS touch icon are redrawn from the mascot on the home page's mint-to-sky
gradient; manifest colours follow the new cream background.

The accessibility audit script now waits for elements instead of clicking
at once (one state failed on a slow page); the full audit passes.

Codex fix batches A + D: install integrity and renderer performance

Batch A (downloads/installer, from the gpt-6.1-sol review):
- Folder ownership markers; cancel only deletes folders the job created
- Cancel/pause await the run, drain chunk workers, close handles; generation
  IDs stop late progress from overwriting paused/queued state
- Every existing-file replacement is staged; resume entries bound to the
  manifest hash and size-checked; manifests written atomically
- Short writes looped and verified; streamed bandwidth throttling with no
  oversized bypass; 128 MiB hard chunk-memory budget with eviction
- Path-boundary checks against junction/symlink escapes; bounded manifest
  and chunk parsing; third-party titles skipped by auto-update
- 19 offline regression tests (npm test)

Batch D (renderer):
- Row-virtualized library grid and windowed shelves (600 games: ~48 tiles
  mounted instead of 600, ~615 DOM nodes on Home)
- Shared entity indexes and keyed subscriptions; GamePage, collections and
  route CSS lazy-loaded (startup CSS 112 KB -> 74 KB)
- Store unload on idle/game start/hidden window, URL restore, crash reload
- Properties tab, bootstrap snapshot, storage and collection-edit fixes
- 9 renderer regression tests
